info.name: CourtMesh API: Indian Court Cases
info.description:
# CourtMesh API: Indian court cases

A REST API over Indian court judgments and orders: the Supreme Court, every High Court, District Courts and tribunals. Search by keyword or by meaning, pull a single judgment with its parties and bench, read a structured AI analysis, follow a matter's order sheet over time, and download the source PDF.

Base URL: `https://research.courtmesh.ai/api/v1/prod`

## Getting a key

API keys are issued from the CourtMesh dashboard at https://research.courtmesh.ai. A key looks like `cm-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX-XXXX`. Keys issued before the rename start with `vv-` and still work.

## Authentication

Every endpoint except `GET /health` needs a key. Two header forms are accepted:

```
Authorization: Bearer cm-your-key-here
```

```
X-API-Key: cm-your-key-here
```

This collection uses the bearer form at the collection level, so set the `apiKey` variable once and every request inherits it.

## Collection variables

| variable | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| baseUrl | API root. Defaults to the production host |
| apiKey | Your API key. Leave it out of source control, use a Postman environment |
| caseId | A case identifier used by the case level requests. Accepts a Mongo ObjectId or a case number |
| requestId | A timeline job id returned by POST /request-timeline |
| userId | A user id for GET /audit's userId query param. Call GET /me first to get your own id |

## Response envelope

Every endpoint except `GET /health` returns:

```json
{ "success": true, "data": {}, "meta": {}, "pagination": {} }
```

`meta` and `pagination` appear only where the endpoint provides them. Failures return `{ "success": false, "error": "..." }`, with an extra `details` array of human readable messages when request validation failed.

Authentication and rate limit failures come from middleware and are not wrapped, they are a bare `{ "error": "..." }`.

Every response, success or failure, carries an `X-Request-Id` response header. Some endpoints (for example `GET /usage`, `POST /party/screen/batch`) also echo it as `meta.requestId` in the body; quote either one when reporting a problem to CourtMesh support.

## Rate limits

10 requests per minute per API key. Successful responses carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`. A 429 body carries `retryAfter` in seconds and `resetTime` as an ISO timestamp. Back off and retry, do not hammer.

## Pagination

Two shapes, because the two search endpoints sit on different engines.

`POST /search/cases` returns `{ total, hasMore, page, limit, nextCursor }`. There is no `totalPages`. For deep pagination, send the previous `nextCursor` back as `searchAfter`, in which case `page` is omitted from the response.

`POST /search/cases/semantic` returns `{ page, limit, total, totalPages, hasMore }`, where `total` and `totalPages` are estimates that only become exact on the final page.

## Idempotency

POST /party/screen, POST /party/screen/batch, POST /cases/{id}/analyze, POST /cases/{id}/analyze-consolidated and POST /request-timeline each accept an optional `Idempotency-Key` header, 1 to 128 characters, `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`. Every request for these five endpoints in this collection carries one, defaulted to Postman's `{{$guid}}` dynamic variable (a fresh UUID v4 generated on every send).

The key is scoped per API key for 24 hours: replaying the same key with the same request body returns the original 2xx response again, with response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, and no new charge. The same key with a different body is refused with 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. A request with this key still being processed is refused with 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`. A malformed key is refused with 400 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID`.

Because `{{$guid}}` regenerates on every send, re-sending one of these requests from the Postman UI runs as a new, separately charged call each time, by design. To deliberately exercise the replay behaviour, replace the header value with a fixed string before sending the same request twice.

| method | path | folder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST | /search/cases | Search |
| POST | /search/cases/semantic | Search |
| GET | /cases/{id} | Cases |
| GET | /cases/{id}/related | Cases |
| GET | /cases/{id}/pdf | Cases |
| GET | /cases/{id}/analysis | Analysis |
| POST | /cases/{id}/analyze | Analysis |
| POST | /cases/{id}/analyze-consolidated | Analysis |
| GET | /judges/search | Judges |
| POST | /request-timeline | Timeline |
| GET | /get-timeline/{requestId} | Timeline |
| POST | /party/screen | Litigation Check |
| POST | /party/screen/batch | Litigation Check |
| GET | /usage | Account |
| GET | /me | Account |
| GET | /audit | Account |
| GET | /reference/courts | Reference |
| GET | /reference/case-types | Reference |
| GET | /coverage | Coverage |
| GET | /health | System |
| GET | /health?deep=1 | System |

## Official SDKs

Python: `pip install courtmesh`

Node and TypeScript: `npm install @courtmesh/sdk`

item.name: Search
item.description: Keyword search and semantic search over Indian court judgments.

request.description:
Keyword search across the OpenSearch index of Indian court judgments.

`query` is required and must be at least one character after trimming. Everything else is optional.

Body fields, taken from the zod schema `searchCasesSchema`:

| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| query | string | required, trimmed, minimum length 1 |
| court | string or string array | optional |
| year | integer, a four digit string, or an array of either | optional. Integers must be between 1947 and the current year |
| caseType | string or string array | optional. Values are expanded to court case type codes server side |
| caseNumber | string, or a one element string array | optional. Filters results on that single case number; a second array element is rejected with 400 ("Only one caseNumber can be filtered per request."), never silently dropped |
| judgeName | string or string array | optional |
| judges | string or string array | optional alias for judgeName |
| judge | string or string array | optional alias for judgeName |
| fromDate | string | optional, format YYYY-MM-DD |
| toDate | string | optional, format YYYY-MM-DD |
| page | integer | optional, minimum 1, default 1 |
| limit | integer | optional, 1 to 100, default 20. Each plan tier caps this lower (Free tier: 20); above the cap is rejected with 400 `PAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, and `page * limit` beyond the tier's pagination depth cap is rejected with 400 `PAGINATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` |
| cursor | string | optional opaque signed pagination cursor, the current mechanism. Send the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` back unmodified to fetch the next page; a cursor issued for a different query/filters, or a malformed one, is rejected with 400 `CURSOR_INVALID` |
| searchAfter | string | optional legacy cursor, honoured only while the server's self serve API tiers feature is off. Prefer `cursor` above for new integrations |
| sortBy | "relevance", "recent" or "oldest" | optional, default "relevance". "date" is accepted too, as a deprecated alias that is applied as "recent" |

Judge precedence in the handler is judgeName, then judges, then judge.

Response `data` is an array of raw search hits. Each hit carries the indexed document fields plus `_id`, `_score` and `_sort`. Full judgment text is not stored in the index, so `detailedSummary`, `holding`, `keyFacts_joined`, `legalIssues_joined` and `courtsReasoning` never appear here. Fetch a single case with GET /cases/{id} for the curated view.

Pagination on this endpoint is `{ total, hasMore, page, limit, nextCursor }`. There is no `totalPages`. `page` is omitted when you paginate with `cursor` or the legacy `searchAfter`.

`caseNumber` and `sortBy` are both real, honoured filters today: `caseNumber` narrows results to that single case number, and `relevance`, `recent` and `oldest` are all real sort orders (`date` silently maps to `recent`, and the response's `meta` carries a notice explaining the substitution).

{
  "query": "trade licence cancelled without notice",
  "court": "Bombay High Court",
  "year": 2021,
  "caseType": "WP",
  "judgeName": "Deshpande",
  "fromDate": "2020-01-01",
  "toDate": "2021-12-31",
  "page": 1,
  "limit": 20,
  "sortBy": "relevance"
}

request.description:
List every stored document that shares this case's case number, plus a derived hearing timeline.

The `id` path parameter accepts either a Mongo ObjectId string or a case number. The handler tries the ObjectId lookup first and falls back to a case number lookup.

`data.relatedDocuments` is capped at 50 documents and each entry carries `id`, `title`, `caseNumber`, `court`, `decisionDate` as YYYY-MM-DD, `caseType` and `isCurrent`. The list is returned newest first.

`data.timeline` only includes documents that have both a decision date and a stored PDF, sorted oldest first. Each event carries `date`, `status`, `statusLabel` and `documentId`. `status` is one of "Final Judgment", "Hearings / Orders" or "Case Initiated". The earliest event is relabelled "Case Initiated" unless it is already a final judgment. `statusLabel` is the disposal nature when the document has one, otherwise it repeats the status.

When the case has no case number, `data` is `{ "relatedDocuments": [], "timeline": [] }` and `meta.message` explains why.

request.description:
Get an encrypted, presigned download URL for the case PDF.

The `id` path parameter accepts either a Mongo ObjectId string or a case number. The handler tries the ObjectId lookup first and falls back to a case number lookup.

`data.pdfUrl` is ciphertext, not a URL you can fetch directly. It wraps a presigned S3 link that expires after `data.expiresIn` seconds, which is 3600. Decryption uses a case specific key and is handled by the CourtMesh SDKs.

Two distinct 404s: code `CASE_NOT_FOUND` means no case matches `id` at all. Code `PDF_NOT_STORED` means the case exists but has no stored document, and carries a `hint` field pointing at POST /request-timeline with `refresh: true`, which can fetch orders for High Court and District Court cases (tribunal documents are not fetchable via this API).

request.description:
Queue AI analysis for one case. The call returns immediately with 202 and the work continues in the background.

The `id` path parameter accepts either a Mongo ObjectId string or a case number. The handler tries the ObjectId lookup first and falls back to a case number lookup.

Body: `{ "force": false, "allowRemoteFetch": false }`. Both fields are optional and default to false.

`force`: send `true` to re-run analysis on a case that already has one (also billed again).

`allowRemoteFetch`: required before the server will fetch this case's source document from a remote court host, when it is not already available as stored text or an S3 document (only ecourts.gov.in, nic.in, sci.gov.in, gov.in and courtmesh.ai hosts are ever eligible). Without it, a case that needs a remote fetch to be analyzed returns 403 `REMOTE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED` instead of running. When a remote fetch actually happens, a 20 credit surcharge is added on top of the base analyze price. Not available on the Free tier, which returns 403 `REMOTE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED` regardless of this flag.

Responses:
- 202 when the job was queued. `data` is `{ message: "Analysis has been started", status: "processing" }`. Poll GET /cases/{id} and watch `hasAnalysis`, or read GET /cases/{id}/analysis, after 30 to 60 seconds.
- 200 when an analysis already exists and `force` was not set. `data` is `{ message: "Analysis already exists", analysis: { ... }, alreadyExists: true }`.
- 400 when the case has neither at least 100 characters of stored text nor an attached document.
- 403 `API_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED` on the Free tier, which has no AI analysis allowance at all.
- 403 `REMOTE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED` when the document needs a remote fetch and `allowRemoteFetch` was not sent, or the tier does not allow it, or the host is outside the allowed list.

The analysis runs against the stored judgment PDF when one is available, and falls back to the extracted text otherwise.

**Credits.** This call costs 100 credits per run, plus a further 20 credit surcharge when the source document actually had to be fetched remotely, charged when the job is queued; a cached `alreadyExists` response is not charged again. Not available on the free tier: this endpoint, POST /cases/{id}/analyze-consolidated and GET /cases/{id}/analysis all return 403 with code `API_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED` and an upgrade URL on the free tier, which has no AI analysis allowance at all.

request.description:
Run a single AI analysis across the whole matter rather than one document.

The `id` path parameter accepts either a Mongo ObjectId string or a case number. The handler tries the ObjectId lookup first and falls back to a case number lookup.

Body: `{ "force": false }`. `force` is optional and defaults to false.

Unlike POST /cases/{id}/analyze, this call is synchronous and can take a while. It gathers the documents first:
- High Court matters: the current case plus its five most recent orders.
- Supreme Court matters: up to 20 documents that share the same case number.

The combined text is capped at 100,000 characters. The result is stored, so a second call without `force` returns the stored copy with `status: "already_analyzed"`.

`data.consolidatedAnalysis` carries the same keys as the single case analysis plus `benchComposition`, `opinionType`, `factPattern`, `linkedCases` and `outcome`.

Error cases: 400 when the case has no case number or no usable text, 403 when the account's AI allowance is exhausted, 404 when the case or its related documents cannot be found.

**Credits.** This call costs significantly more than POST /cases/{id}/analyze (400 credits), charged once the analysis completes; a cached `already_analyzed` response is not charged again. request.description:
Read or refresh the order sheet and hearing history for a case.

Body: `{ "case_id": "<Mongo ObjectId>", "refresh": false }`. `case_id` is required and must be an ObjectId string, a case number will not work here. `refresh` is optional and defaults to false.

`refresh: false` (default) is a STORED read: 1 credit, `meta.liveFetch` is `false`, and it never contacts a court portal. `refresh: true` forces a LIVE fetch directly from the court's own systems instead: 20 credits, `meta.liveFetch` is `true`, available on the PAYG tier and above only (Free tier returns 403 `LIVE_FETCH_NOT_ALLOWED`), and subject to a per tier daily cap (429 `LIVE_FETCH_LIMIT_REACHED` once exhausted, with `retryAfter` telling you when it resets).

The response tells you what happened:
- `status: "pending"` with a `requestId`. A background job was queued. Poll GET /get-timeline/{requestId}.
- `status: "completed"` with `cached: true`, `orders` and `orderCount`. Orders were already fetched today, so you get them straight back.
- `status: "completed"` with `orderCount: 0` and an explanatory `message` for Supreme Court cases, which do not have separate orders. The case document is itself the judgment.
- `status: "failed"` with a `message`, for example when a District Court case has no CNR.

Order objects carry `_id`, `title`, `caseNumber`, `decisionDate`, `court`, `caseType`, `disposalNature`, `judges`, `judge`, `petitioners`, `respondents`, `hasS3Key`, `s3Key` and `s3Bucket`.

request.description:
Corpus coverage and freshness snapshot: total records, a breakdown by court type and by year, per court figures, and a rolled up District Court row (the index has no state field for district courts yet).

No API key required. Cached server side, see `meta.cacheTtlSeconds`; treat `data.generatedAt` as the figure's as-of time rather than expecting a live count on every call.

Each row (`byCourtType`, `courts`, `districtCourts`) uses `records` for its count, not `total`. `documentBearing` (a count of records that also have the order or judgment text indexed) and, at the top level only, `statusOnly` are OPTIONAL and OMITTED BY DEFAULT at every level they could appear (top level, each `byCourtType` row, each `courts` row, `districtCourts`) - the document-bearing versus status-only split is behind a publish flag (`COVERAGE_PUBLISH_DOCUMENT_SHARE`, default off) and is not disclosed until a human turns it on, so do not assume it is present.

request.description:
Deep health check. The plain GET /health above is a cheap liveness probe, no dependency calls, always fast, always 200 while the process is up. Adding ?deep=1 also checks Mongo, OpenSearch, Qdrant, Redis and IAM standing (each bounded to 1 second) and returns a checks object, one entry per dependency: { status: "ok" | "degraded" | "down", latencyMs, error? }.
